g.text: 18 093 us start; 30.0 us host window; sample 45 us into the release, margins 17.0 / 25.0 us
1. the start signal: the host resets the sensor
The idle state is the pull-up. Open-drain is
deliberately NOT set: the 30 us high below is a
timed interval in the project, 6.4x the WS2812
reset and 900x the WS2812 bit cell. This is what
forces a three-level delay routine: as NOPs it
would not fit in 1 024 words of instruction memory.
0.5 % long, and that is the RIGHT DIRECTION for a
minimum: a start signal that is too short is a reset
2. the host's high window: a driven high, then a RELEASE
This middle step is NOT OPTIONAL. The sensor pulls
its own line low to answer, so the host cannot just
stop driving and let the pull-up win - the sensor
would see a line that never went high and would not
start converting. Pulling it high for 30 us
guarantees a clean high-to-low transition to answer
with, and only then does the host become a reader.
THE TB MEASURES THE RELEASE ON pin_oe, NOT ON THE LINE.
The host drives high and then releases, and the
pull-up holds the line high throughout, so on the
WIRE the release moves nothing at all. A TB that
looks for a falling edge here waits forever or, if
it is looking for the wrong thing, measures the
window from a transition that is not one.
the line does NOT fall on the release -
the pull-up already holds it high
3. the acknowledge: 80 low, 80 high, NEVER TIMED
The firmware does not time this. It falls into the
SAME edge-wait loop it uses for bits: the first round
waits out the acknowledge, the second one is bit 0.
Nothing on the wire announces when the acknowledge is
over, so timing it would be another delay constant to
fit and another place to be wrong. One loop, two uses.
4. bit 0: the value IS the width
has one, so the host cannot use it as the value.
w_lo: spin until the line is LOW
a spin loop on the pin, polling every three
instructions, so an edge is caught within 50 ns
against a 26 us window - four thousand times finer
w_hi: spin until the line is HIGH
datasheet's 26-28 us window. A sensor inside its
own specification, and the TB drives this on
purpose so the margin is measured against the
worst legal sensor rather than the typical one.
THE SAMPLE: 17.0 us of margin on the 0 side.
The 0's release has already ENDED and the next bit
has pulled the line low again.
A sample at 20 us would be INSIDE the release, where
a 0 and a 1 are indistinguishable - the mutation
case dh-sample-instant moves it to 14 us and the
the same two waits, then 45 us
25.0 us of margin on the 1 side.
The 1's release is still running, so the line is
... 40 bits. 24 of the 39 bit-transitions are real,
which is the TB's non-vacuity floor: a frame of
all-0s or all-1s would make a width-based decoder
trivially correct and the check would prove nothing.
after the fortieth bit, the line released,
the sensor left alone, and the firmware parks with dmem[15] = 1.
the timing table, and what each window protects
|= what |= required |= produced | which side | what it protects |=
a clean high-to-low for the sensor to answer
nothing to see on the line: the pull-up already holds it high
skipped by the edge loop, not fitted
the worst legal sensor, so the margin is real
Why the 45 us is AIMED and the other numbers are only SATISFIED.
and the host window have bands, and landing anywhere inside them is correct. The
sample has no band: it has to be after the 0's release ENDS and before the 1's
release ENDS, because inside the release the line is high for both values. That is
the one number in this program that has a target rather than a range, and it is the
FINE pair that makes it aimable - with the coarse (6,255) step, 20.7 us would be
inside the host window and 34 us would be outside it, so neither could be aimed at
Why the margins are asymmetric, and why that is the sensor's doing.
0 side, 25 us on the 1 side. The 0's release is 26-28 us and the 1's is ~70 us, so
a sample aimed at the MIDDLE of the gap would sit at 49 us - 21 us of margin on the
0 side and 21 on the 1. 45 us trades the 0's margin for the 1's, which is the right
trade: the 0's window is 14x tighter than the sample's precision, and the 1's is not.
